title: AI, ML & Data Science: Foundations
description: Mixed-format quiz (MCQ, true/false, select-all) on what AI is, ANI/AGI/ASI, ML vs traditional programming, and how AI, ML, Deep Learning & Data Science relate — aligned with the university question bank (Q1–Q3) and Chapter 1 of the course guide.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of Artificial Intelligence?
options: To develop systems that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence
To build the fastest possible arithmetic calculators
To replace all data storage systems with cloud servers
questions.answer: To develop systems that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence

questions.question: Unlike a calculator, which only follows fixed arithmetic rules, what is an AI system expected to do?
options: Handle situations that were not explicitly programmed in advance, by generalizing or adapting
Fail immediately on any unfamiliar input
questions.answer: Handle situations that were not explicitly programmed in advance, by generalizing or adapting

questions.question: Who coined the term "Artificial Intelligence" at the 1956 Dartmouth Conference, marking the field's formal founding?
Which term describes AI systems built and trained to perform one specific task well, such as recommending movies or detecting spam — and which describes almost every AI system in use today?
Which term describes a theoretical form of AI that could understand, learn, and apply intelligence to any intellectual task a human can, transferring knowledge flexibly across domains?
Which term describes a hypothetical stage where a machine's intelligence would exceed human intelligence in essentially every respect, relevant mainly to long-term AI safety research?
In traditional programming, what does a human programmer provide the computer, and what does the computer produce?
options: Rules + input → the computer produces output
Input + output examples → the computer produces rules
Only output, with no input needed
questions.answer: Rules + input → the computer produces output

questions.question: In Machine Learning, what is the system given, and what does it produce on its own?
options: Input + output examples → the system produces (learns) the rules
Rules + input → the system produces output
Only rules, with no data at all
A fixed answer key that is never used
questions.answer: Input + output examples → the system produces (learns) the rules

questions.question: When does Machine Learning become essential instead of traditional programming?
options: When the true rule is too complex, too subtle, or simply unknown for a human to write down directly
When the task only ever involves basic arithmetic
When no data is available at all
When the rule is simple and already known in advance
questions.answer: When the true rule is too complex, too subtle, or simply unknown for a human to write down directly

questions.question: Among Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Data Science, which is described as the broadest of the three fields?
How is Deep Learning classified relative to Machine Learning?
options: Deep Learning is a subset of Machine Learning that uses multi-layered neural networks
Deep Learning is broader than Machine Learning
Deep Learning and Machine Learning are completely unrelated fields
Deep Learning is a subset of Data Science only, unrelated to ML
questions.answer: Deep Learning is a subset of Machine Learning that uses multi-layered neural networks

questions.question: How is Data Science described in relation to Machine Learning?
options: A broader, more applied practice that frequently uses ML as just one of its tools
A narrower subset contained entirely within ML
Identical to ML, with no meaningful difference
A field that never involves statistics
questions.answer: A broader, more applied practice that frequently uses ML as just one of its tools

questions.question: Almost every AI system in active use today, including ANNs, CNNs, and RNNs, is an example of Narrow AI (ANI).
A Narrow AI system that is excellent at chess automatically gains the ability to hold a conversation, because its intelligence transfers across tasks.
In Machine Learning, the model's internal decision logic is learned from data rather than explicitly hand-written by a programmer.
AGI (human-level general intelligence) already exists today and is deployed in common smartphone apps.
Which of the following are true when comparing Machine Learning to traditional programming?
options: ML's behavior can improve automatically as more data is provided
Traditional programming struggles with complex, unclear, or fuzzy problems
In ML, the rules (patterns) are hand-written by the programmer
In traditional programming, a new situation requires the programmer to add new rules
answer: ML's behavior can improve automatically as more data is provided
Traditional programming struggles with complex, unclear, or fuzzy problems
In traditional programming, a new situation requires the programmer to add new rules

questions.question: Which of the following are among the three objective-based "types" of AI, classified by their level of capability?
Which of the following are part of the "scope of AI" — the range of capabilities AI aims to cover?
Which of the following are application areas within the scope of AI?
